extraChanges.change: The PDF-to-HTML adapter emits finite diagnostic codes through the M1 catalog; raw HTML engine emissions remain owned by the adapter.
extraChanges.reason: PDF reconstruction loss tests showed source security and page-label findings retained old literal names.

extraChanges.note: HTML to PDF now exposes ToPdf/out-report, ToPdfAsync and shared-report SaveAsPdf forms; private rendering evidence is retained for adapters and fidelity tests. HtmlPdfExportOptions.FailOnLoss is copied by ClonePdf.

PDF to HTML now exposes string ToHtml/out-report, OfficeConversionResult<string> ToHtmlAsync and shared-report saves. PdfHtmlExportOptions.FailOnLoss rejects before publication and is captured in conversion options.

The M1 inventory omitted 36 finite PDF-to-HTML warning codes. Added them to diagnostic-code-map.json and generated OfficeDiagnosticCodes, applied constants at emission sites and migrated contract assertions. No severity, location or loss-kind changes.

Async conversion entry points capture options before deferred work or resource awaits. The same snapshot supplies resource/size limits and final FailOnLoss acceptance; caller-owned template documents and callbacks retain their ownership.

Strict adapter PDF saves use the existing staged writer with shared report acceptance before publication. Source-stage and writer-time losses throw OfficeConversionException carrying OfficeConversionReport; native advanced result policies keep their existing behavior. The same writer and file/stream publication owners are reused. Front-door HTML/TXT saves dispose the generated model.

Public ToPdf and SaveAsPdf families keep serialization and publication inside the same render deadline as resource resolution and layout. The existing HtmlRenderEngine deadline owner and PdfConversionEvidence writers remain authoritative.
Canonical SaveAs output failures retain the completed conversion report through the shared internal output helper; cancellation continues to propagate unchanged.
HTML PDF saves validate destination arguments before rendering. Both synchronous and asynchronous final writes retain completed reports through the shared PDF evidence owner.

HTML row/cell traversal and serialized shadow-root traversal enumerate AngleSharp collections rather than binding their target-specific indexer member. This fixes MissingMethodException when a netstandard2.0 adapter is loaded with the runtime-selected modern AngleSharp asset, preserves traversal order and keeps linear traversal.

InternalsVisibleTo grants the existing browser engine and its tests access to detailed conversion and serialization evidence. This preserves browser diagnostics while keeping conversion kernels outside the public API.

applicationStatus: Phase A applied and validated on macOS, including standard-library and modern-framework runtime proof. Windows .NET Framework validation remains pending.
authority: Docs/officeimo.api-design.md, including the c526a10ad2 framework decision; the approved design overrides M0 open questions.

questionResolutions.conversionForms: Source.ToTarget, source.SaveAsTarget and OfficeConversionReport; async ToTarget returns OfficeConversionResult<T>. ToHtml returns string. No static From factories.
questionResolutions.frameworks: No framework is dropped in 3.6. Original library TFMs and Windows net472 conditions remain; the front door and both Workflows projects support the full set. Modern-only engines stay conditional.
questionResolutions.packageDirection: Word.Pdf and PowerPoint.Pdf export native documents. Reverse reconstruction is Pdf.Word and Pdf.PowerPoint; Excel reconstruction is Pdf.Excel. Word page images live in Word.Pdf.
questionResolutions.surface: Markdown syntax nodes are exempt from the format prefix. OfficeColor/OfficeColorRole use the root OfficeIMO namespace. Authoring, units, image-builder consolidation, visibility baselines and AOT smoke acceptance are Phase B.
